title: Japanese City Accused of Adding 2,000 Fake Residents
paragraphs: Workers at a city office in Japan are suspected of adding at least 2,000 people who do not exist to the city's population count.

The city is Toyama, in central Japan. Every five years, Japan holds a national census to count everyone who lives in the country. According to Japan's internal affairs ministry, Toyama's population in the 2025 census was made larger than it really was by at least 2,000 people.

The ministry found problems with the city's numbers. It then asked the police to investigate several unnamed city workers. On October 3, 2026, about 10 police investigators searched the Toyama City Office. They are investigating whether the workers broke Japan's law on statistics.
At first, the city's population was reported as 402,133. Later, the final number was changed to 399,197.

The wrong number may have cost the national government money. The early census number was used to decide how much money Toyama would get from the national government. The city thinks it may have received about 60 million yen more than it should have.

Some people wondered if the city wanted to keep its population above 400,000. But Toyama's mayor, Hirohisa Fujii, said this was not the reason. Fujii also said there were no instructions from senior officials, and that the city would fully cooperate with the police. The mayor also promised to take responsibility for the problem at the right time.
